# NITRR Digital Twin - Copilot Instructions

## Project

We are building a full-stack application called NITRR Digital Twin.

It is a campus intelligence and digital twin platform for
National Institute of Technology Raipur.

The application represents campus locations, facilities,
resources, events, activity and simulated campus conditions.

## Developer

The developer is learning full-stack development.

Use simple, readable and maintainable code.

Do not use unnecessary abstractions or complicated patterns.

## Technology Stack

Frontend:
- React
- Vite
- JavaScript
- Tailwind CSS
- React Router
- Axios
- Leaflet
- Recharts
- Socket.IO Client

Backend:
- Node.js
- Express
- MongoDB
- Mongoose
- JWT
- bcryptjs
- Zod
- Socket.IO

## Main Features

1. Authentication
2. Student and admin roles
3. Campus locations
4. Interactive campus map
5. Location details
6. Events
7. Resource availability
8. Smart Finder
9. Resource sharing
10. Issue reporting
11. Campus activity
12. Campus pressure calculation
13. Admin dashboard
14. Analytics
15. Real-time updates
16. Future prediction capabilities

## Development Rules

1. Do not build the entire application at once.
2. Work feature by feature.
3. Inspect existing files before modifying them.
4. Do not modify unrelated files.
5. Do not install unnecessary dependencies.
6. Explain why a dependency is required.
7. Never hardcode passwords or secrets.
8. Use environment variables for secrets.
9. Validate backend input.
10. Validate frontend forms.
11. Never trust frontend authorization.
12. Implement authorization on the backend.
13. Use appropriate HTTP status codes.
14. Handle loading states.
15. Handle error states.
16. Handle empty states.
17. Avoid duplicated code.
18. Do not hide errors.
19. Do not suppress warnings simply to make code appear to work.
20. Do not create fake APIs.
21. Clearly identify simulated data.
22. Do not claim simulated occupancy is real sensor data.
23. Do not invent official NIT Raipur statistics.
24. Use verified information for real NIT Raipur data.
25. Test every feature before declaring it complete.

## Development Workflow

Always follow:

PLAN
→ IMPLEMENT
→ RUN
→ TEST
→ DEBUG
→ VERIFY
→ COMMIT

Before implementing a large feature:

1. Inspect the existing project.
2. Explain the implementation plan.
3. Identify files that will change.
4. Identify required dependencies.
5. Implement incrementally.

After implementation:

1. Run the application.
2. Test the feature.
3. Run the relevant build/tests.
4. Fix errors.
5. Check for regressions.
6. Report what was changed.

Never say a feature is complete merely because code was generated.

A feature is complete only after it has been tested.
